title: Basket
subtitle: Risk-based weights and vol targeting on the S&P 500 top-50
headline: Tuesday 10 November 2026. Risk parity (ERC) basket: 10.9% ex-ante vol, 41 effective bets, Mag 7 13% of weight for 15% of risk. Realized 22d vol 17.2% (high), VIX 19.5: the 10% vol target sets leverage at 0.58x. Top idea: equal weight, unlevered.

sections.title: Today's basket
paragraphs: Risk parity (ERC) on the 43 largest S&P 500 names, Ledoit-Wolf covariance on 252 days (shrinkage intensity 0.055, average pairwise correlation 0.11), 10% cap per name and 30% cap on the Mag 7. Ex-ante vol 10.9%, 41.0 effective bets, diversification ratio 2.78.
The Mag 7 take 13% of the weight and 15% of the risk; cap-weighting would hold them at 54%. Largest position KO at 6.3%. Largest sector by risk: Technology (32% of risk for 21% of weight).

The sample covariance of 43 names on 252 days has a condition number of 513; shrinking toward the constant-correlation target brings it to 341. That is why min variance holds 25 names instead of five.

sections.title: Leverage and regime
paragraphs: The Risk parity (ERC) basket realized 17.2% over the last 22 sessions, the 81th percentile since 2015 (high); VIX at 19.5. A 10% vol target sets tomorrow's leverage at 0.58x (cap 2.0x, average 1.01x over the backtest): de-lever, realized vol is above target.

Over 11 years the overlay added +0.18 of Sharpe on average across the six schemes and cut the average worst drawdown from -31% to -15%. The spread of Sharpe between the six schemes is 0.17: the vol target moves the result more than the weights.
On 10 Nov the basket returned +0.20% against -0.37% for SPY and -0.03% for RSP, the equal-weight S&P 500 ETF (12% a year over the window against 15% for equal weight on the point-in-time top 50).

ideas.thesis: The naive basket: +1.66% over the following month in this regime (67% positive, worst -19.3%). Backtests use a point-in-time universe: on today's survivors equal weight would have made about 26% a year instead of 15%.

method: Ideas are the baskets to hold this month, ranked by historical conditional expectation (next 21 days) divided by the historical worst case in the same regime. Conditioning variable: the quartile of the basket's trailing 22-day realized vol.
caveats: Point-in-time universe: monthly top N by today's float shares times that month's price; share-count changes and names delisted since are not captured. Today's basket (first section) uses today's names.
Conditional returns are averages over overlapping 21-day windows; they describe the regime, not a forecast.
Costs: 5 bps per unit of turnover, including leverage changes. No financing cost on leverage above 1.
